Meeting Personalities: B2 Lesson

B2 ESL Connect Video lesson based on the tapescript: brainstorming, difficult participants, meeting control, note-taking and action points.

Video link: Open on YouTube

Lesson Aim

Students watch a comic video about unproductive meeting behaviours and practise language for managing brainstorming, interruptions, time pressure, note-taking and difficult participants.

Before watching

  1. What makes meetings unproductive?
  2. What types of difficult meeting participants have you seen?
  3. How can a leader keep a brainstorming session under control?

B2 Grammar · Reported Speech

Use reported speech to pass on what people said after a meeting.

  • Statements. Use said (that) or told + person + (that). When reporting a past conversation, tenses often shift back: am/is → was, are → were, past simple → past perfect, will → would. If the information is still true or relevant, backshift can be optional.
  • Questions. Use asked if/whether for yes/no questions and keep the question word in wh-questions. Use statement word order: She asked how long the meeting would last.
  • Instructions and suggestions. Use told/asked + person + to + verb for instructions or requests, and suggested + -ing for suggestions.
  • Reference words. Update pronouns and time expressions when the context changes: “I’ll send you the notes tomorrow” → She told us she would send us the notes the following day.

Report what was said

Imagine you are describing the meeting later. Choose the best reported version and use backshift where appropriate.

1. Tyler said, “We’re just brainstorming.”
Tyler said that they ___ just brainstorming.

2. Tripp said, “It’ll be on Facebook.”
Tripp said that it ___ on Facebook.

3. The late participant said, “I got caught in traffic.”
He explained that he ___ caught in traffic.

4. Tyler asked Tripp, “Are you ready to get started?”
Tyler asked Tripp ___ ready to get started.

5. Nancy asked, “How are you going to plan around the weather?”
Nancy asked the team how ___ to plan around the weather.

6. Tripp told the team, “Call the IT guy.”
Tripp told the team ___ the IT guy.

7. Nancy said, “I think we should implement Pinterest.”
Nancy suggested ___ Pinterest.

8. Practice example: Maya said to us, “I’ll send you the notes tomorrow.”
Reporting this a week later: Maya told us that ___ the notes the following day.

Thought-Provoking Questions

1. Which meeting personality from the video is the most damaging?

2. Is it better to stop bad ideas immediately or encourage all ideas first?

3. How should a leader deal with someone who dominates?

4. How detailed should meeting notes be?

5. Should meetings always have a strict time limit?

6. What technology problems often waste time in meetings?

7. What makes a brainstorming session successful?

Context

Situation: Your team is brainstorming a marketing campaign, but the meeting is becoming chaotic.

Student A

You are the meeting leader. Keep people focused, stop interruptions politely and make sure there are clear action points.

Student B

You are a difficult participant. Choose one behaviour: dominate, criticise every idea, arrive late, or ramble.

Role play task: Finish the meeting with one campaign idea, one owner and one next step.
